Explainable Multimodal Airbnb Price Prediction¶

Reproduction-inspired study based on Tan et al. (2024) — Kaggle T4¶

Project objective. Reconstruct a three-branch price prediction system using (1) listing metadata, (2) listing text, and (3) the host-provided cover photo, then audit its decisions with explainable AI.

Reference paper: Tan, H. et al. (2024), A Sustainable Rental Price Prediction Model Based on Multimodal Input and Deep Learning—Evidence from Airbnb, Sustainability 16(15), 6384. DOI: 10.3390/su16156384.

Important reproducibility note. The paper reports 8,380 Amsterdam listings collected in April 2024. That historical snapshot and the authors' exact image/text files are not packaged with this notebook. To keep the experiment reproducible and legally traceable, this notebook downloads the currently linked Amsterdam detailed-listings snapshot from Inside Airbnb (configured below), downloads each selected listing's picture_url, and caps the sample at 8,380 rows by default. This is a reproduction-inspired implementation on a newer snapshot, not an exact reproduction of the authors' 2024 experiment. Do not expect the published 5.5682% MAPE to be reproduced.

Source licence. Inside Airbnb publishes its downloadable data under CC BY 4.0 and requests attribution. Cite Inside Airbnb and the research paper in your report.

Arwah Events framing. This is a proxy study for the price estimation / quote preparation stage: estimating nightly accommodation prices from property attributes, descriptions, and photos. Airbnb prices are not event-venue quotes, and Amsterdam is not Tunis. Present this as a transferable multimodal pricing methodology, not as a production pricing model for Arwah Events.

What this notebook does¶

  1. Downloads and validates a real public snapshot; checks the required columns and image availability.
  2. Cleans the target and builds metadata, text, and image inputs.
  3. Splits by host_id to reduce host leakage (train / validation / test).
  4. Trains seven modality combinations, mirroring the paper's ablation design.
  5. Reports MAE, RMSE, R² and MAPE in the source price unit.
  6. Explains the full multimodal model using SHAP, PDP, LIME, Integrated Gradients, Grad-CAM, Occlusion, and exact three-player modality Shapley values.
  7. Includes local faithfulness checks and saves all artifacts.

No results are pre-filled. All metrics and plots are generated only after the downloaded data have been processed and models trained.

0. Kaggle setup¶

In Kaggle: Settings → Accelerator → GPU T4 and turn Internet on. Run cells from top to bottom. If you add the listings CSV manually through Add Input, set LISTINGS_CSV in the configuration cell. The notebook downloads the CSV and cover photos automatically if Internet access is available.

1. Download / load the public Inside Airbnb listing table¶

The detailed listings file is used because it contains structured attributes, the listing description, and a picture_url field for the cover image. The exact available columns can change across snapshots, so all feature selection below is schema-aware.

In [4]:
def locate_listings_file():
    if LISTINGS_CSV:
        p = Path(LISTINGS_CSV)
        if p.exists(): return p
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"LISTINGS_CSV does not exist: {p}")
    # Look in Kaggle input first, then the working directory.
    candidates = list(Path("/kaggle/input").rglob("listings.csv.gz")) if Path("/kaggle/input").exists() else []
    candidates += list(Path("/kaggle/input").rglob("listings.csv")) if Path("/kaggle/input").exists() else []
    candidates += [ROOT / "listings.csv.gz", ROOT / "listings.csv"]
    for p in candidates:
        if p.exists() and p.is_file(): return p
    return None

listings_path = locate_listings_file()
if listings_path is None:
    target = ROOT / "listings.csv.gz"
    print("Downloading:", LISTINGS_URL)
    response = requests.get(LISTINGS_URL, timeout=120, headers={"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0 research notebook"})
    response.raise_for_status()
    target.write_bytes(response.content)
    listings_path = target

2. Data audit and feature engineering¶

We predict the listing's displayed nightly price. To avoid direct target leakage, price, listing IDs, URLs, host IDs, estimated revenue, and estimated occupancy are not model inputs. Host IDs are used only for group splitting. Potentially post-outcome reputation fields are retained to mirror the paper's reputation-attribute group; this is discussed as a limitation because a static listing snapshot is not a strict prospective quote-time dataset.

In [5]:
def parse_price(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    s = str(x).strip().replace(",", "")
    nums = re.findall(r"[-+]?\d*\.?\d+", s)
    return float(nums[0]) if nums else np.nan

def parse_percent(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    s = str(x).strip()
    if s in {"", "nan", "None"}: return np.nan
    try:
        return float(s.replace("%", "")) / (100.0 if "%" in s else 1.0)
    except Exception:
        return np.nan

def parse_bathrooms(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return np.nan
    m = re.search(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", str(x))
    return float(m.group()) if m else np.nan

def safe_text(x):
    if pd.isna(x): return ""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(x)).strip()

# Work on a copy and create an explicit target.
df = df_raw.copy()
df["price_original"] = df["price"].astype(str)
df["price_target"] = df["price"].map(parse_price)
df = df[(df["price_target"].notna()) & (df["price_target"] > 0) & (df["price_target"] <= 5000)].copy()
df = df[df["picture_url"].notna()].copy()
df["picture_url"] = df["picture_url"].astype(str)
df = df[~df["picture_url"].isin(["", "nan", "None"])].copy()
if "id" in df.columns: df = df.drop_duplicates("id")

text_fields = [c for c in ["name", "description", "neighborhood_overview", "host_about"] if c in df.columns]
df["text_input"] = df[text_fields].fillna("").astype(str).agg(" ".join, axis=1).map(safe_text)
df = df[df["text_input"].str.len() >= 10].copy()

# Parse percent-valued fields; derive consistent numeric indicators.
for c in ["host_response_rate", "host_acceptance_rate"]:
    if c in df.columns: df[c] = df[c].map(parse_percent)
if "bathrooms" not in df.columns and "bathrooms_text" in df.columns:
    df["bathrooms_numeric"] = df["bathrooms_text"].map(parse_bathrooms)
if "bathrooms" in df.columns:
    df["bathrooms_numeric"] = pd.to_numeric(df["bathrooms"], errors="coerce")
if "amenities" in df.columns:
    df["amenities_count"] = df["amenities"].fillna("[]").astype(str).map(lambda s: len(re.findall(r'"[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"', s)))

# Convert common boolean strings to categorical values, not ordinal numbers.
for c in ["host_is_superhost", "host_identity_verified", "host_has_profile_pic", "instant_bookable"]:
    if c in df.columns:
        df[c] = df[c].astype("string").fillna("unknown")

# Date-derived features use listing's scrape date when available; otherwise the snapshot date.
reference = pd.to_datetime(df["last_scraped"], errors="coerce") if "last_scraped" in df.columns else pd.Series(pd.Timestamp(SNAPSHOT_DATE), index=df.index)
if "host_since" in df.columns:
    host_since = pd.to_datetime(df["host_since"], errors="coerce")
    df["host_tenure_days"] = (reference - host_since).dt.days.clip(lower=0)
for src, dest in [("first_review", "days_since_first_review"), ("last_review", "days_since_last_review")]:
    if src in df.columns:
        dt = pd.to_datetime(df[src], errors="coerce")
        df[dest] = (reference - dt).dt.days.clip(lower=0)

# Candidate metadata variables (roughly aligned to the paper's five attribute groups).
numeric_candidates = [
    "host_listings_count", "host_total_listings_count", "host_response_rate", "host_acceptance_rate",
    "accommodates", "bathrooms_numeric", "bedrooms", "beds", "minimum_nights", "maximum_nights",
    "minimum_minimum_nights", "maximum_minimum_nights", "minimum_maximum_nights", "maximum_maximum_nights",
    "availability_30", "availability_60", "availability_90", "availability_365",

    "review_scores_communication", "review_scores_location", "review_scores_value",
    "calculated_host_listings_count", "calculated_host_listings_count_entire_homes",
    "calculated_host_listings_count_private_rooms", "calculated_host_listings_count_shared_rooms",
    "latitude", "longitude", "amenities_count", "host_tenure_days", "days_since_first_review", "days_since_last_review"
]
categorical_candidates = [
    "host_is_superhost", "host_identity_verified", "host_has_profile_pic", "host_response_time",
    "property_type", "room_type", "bathrooms_text", "neighbourhood_cleansed",
    "neighbourhood_group_cleansed", "instant_bookable", "cancellation_policy", "license"
]
numeric_cols = [c for c in numeric_candidates if c in df.columns and pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce").notna().sum() > 20]
categorical_cols = [c for c in categorical_candidates if c in df.columns and df[c].nunique(dropna=True) > 1]

# Ensure model-friendly numeric dtype.
for c in numeric_cols:
    df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce")

print("Rows after basic cleaning:", len(df))

3. Download cover images¶

The detailed Inside Airbnb file supplies a picture_url. We download one featured/cover image per listing, matching the paper's use of one image per listing. Broken or unavailable URLs are recorded; listings without a valid downloaded image are excluded from the strictly multimodal experiment rather than assigned a fake image.

In [6]:
if MAX_LISTINGS is not None and len(df) > MAX_LISTINGS:
    # Deterministic sample; target distribution is not used to stratify regression samples.
    df = df.sample(n=MAX_LISTINGS, random_state=SEED).copy()

def image_filename(row):
    key = str(row.get("id", row.name))
    return IMAGE_DIR / f"{key}.jpg"

def download_one(args):
    idx, url, path = args
    if path.exists() and path.stat().st_size > 2000:
        try:
            with Image.open(path) as im: im.verify()
            return idx, str(path), True
        except Exception:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    try:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT, headers={"User-Agent":"Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; academic research)"})
        r.raise_for_status()
        if len(r.content) < 2000: return idx, None, False
        path.write_bytes(r.content)
        with Image.open(path) as im:
            im.verify()
        return idx, str(path), True
    except Exception:
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        return idx, None, False

jobs = []
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    jobs.append((idx, row["picture_url"], image_filename(row)))
if MAX_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD is not None:
    jobs = jobs[:MAX_IMAGE_DOWNLOAD]
results = []
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=IMAGE_WORKERS) as ex:
    futures = [ex.submit(download_one, job) for job in jobs]
    for f in tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures), desc="Downloading cover images"):
        results.append(f.result())
img_map = {idx: path for idx, path, ok in results if ok}
df["image_path"] = df.index.map(img_map)
valid_image_df = df[df["image_path"].notna()].copy()
print(f"Image download success: {len(valid_image_df):,}/{len(df):,} ({len(valid_image_df)/max(1,len(df)):.1%})")
print("Rows excluded for missing/broken cover images:", len(df)-len(valid_image_df))
if len(valid_image_df) < 500:
    raise RuntimeError("Fewer than 500 usable listing images. Enable Kaggle Internet, check picture_url access, or add the CSV/images as a Kaggle Input.")
df = valid_image_df

5. Train / validation / test split (grouped by host)¶

We split by host_id so that listings belonging to the same host do not appear across training and evaluation. This is stricter than a random row split and helps limit host-specific leakage. If the host identifier is unavailable, the notebook falls back to a deterministic listing-level split and prints a warning.

In [8]:
indices = np.arange(len(df))
if "host_id" in df.columns and df["host_id"].nunique() >= 10:
    groups = df["host_id"].fillna("missing_host").astype(str).values
    gss_test = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.15, random_state=SEED)
    trainval_idx, test_idx = next(gss_test.split(indices, groups=groups))
    gss_val = GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.1765, random_state=SEED+1)
    tr_rel, va_rel = next(gss_val.split(trainval_idx, groups=groups[trainval_idx]))
    train_idx, val_idx = trainval_idx[tr_rel], trainval_idx[va_rel]
    split_mode = "host-grouped"
else:
    warnings.warn("host_id unavailable / too few groups: using a row-level split.")
    trainval_idx, test_idx = train_test_split(indices, test_size=.15, random_state=SEED)
    train_idx, val_idx = train_test_split(trainval_idx, test_size=.1765, random_state=SEED+1)
    split_mode = "row-level fallback"

train_df = df.iloc[train_idx].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
val_df = df.iloc[val_idx].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
test_df = df.iloc[test_idx].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
print("Split mode:", split_mode)
print("Train / validation / test:", len(train_df), len(val_df), len(test_df))
if "host_id" in df.columns and split_mode == "host-grouped":
    htr, hva, hte = [set(x["host_id"].astype(str)) for x in [train_df,val_df,test_df]]
    print("Host overlap train-val:", len(htr & hva), "train-test:", len(htr & hte), "val-test:", len(hva & hte))

6. Preprocess metadata (fit on training data only)¶

Numerical values are imputed with the training median and standardized. Categorical values are imputed and one-hot encoded. This is the metadata / Dense-network branch. estimated_revenue_l365d and estimated_occupancy_l365d are deliberately excluded because they are post-outcome estimates closely linked to the target price.

In [9]:
num_pipe = Pipeline([("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median", add_indicator=True)), ("scaler", StandardScaler())])
try:
    ohe = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=10, max_categories=30, sparse_output=False)
except TypeError:  # compatibility with older scikit-learn
    ohe = OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", min_frequency=10, max_categories=30, sparse=False)
cat_pipe = Pipeline([("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="constant", fill_value="__MISSING__")), ("onehot", ohe)])
transformers = []
if numeric_cols: transformers.append(("num", num_pipe, numeric_cols))
if categorical_cols: transformers.append(("cat", cat_pipe, categorical_cols))
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer(transformers, remainder="drop", sparse_threshold=0.0)

X_train_tab = np.asarray(preprocessor.fit_transform(train_df), dtype=np.float32)
X_val_tab = np.asarray(preprocessor.transform(val_df), dtype=np.float32)
X_test_tab = np.asarray(preprocessor.transform(test_df), dtype=np.float32)
try:
    tab_feature_names = preprocessor.get_feature_names_out().tolist()
except Exception:
    tab_feature_names = [f"tab_{i}" for i in range(X_train_tab.shape[1])]

y_train = np.log1p(train_df["price_target"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32))
y_val = np.log1p(val_df["price_target"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32))
y_test = np.log1p(test_df["price_target"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32))
print("Tabular matrices:", X_train_tab.shape, X_val_tab.shape, X_test_tab.shape)
print("Expanded metadata features:", len(tab_feature_names))

7. Load pretrained text and image encoders¶

This follows the paper's three-branch idea (Dense metadata + BERT text + MobileNet image). For T4 practicality, the encoders are frozen and their embeddings are extracted once. The fusion/regression heads are trained separately for all seven modality combinations. The final XAI functions still send a selected raw text/image through the frozen encoder with gradients enabled where required.

8. Extract BERT and MobileNet embeddings¶

The text encoder uses the BERT [CLS] representation. The image encoder uses global average pooling of MobileNetV2's final convolutional feature map. This keeps the frozen feature extraction reproducible and allows the seven model variants to share the same embeddings.

In [11]:
def encode_texts(texts, batch_size=32, max_length=MAX_TEXT_LENGTH, keep_model=True):
    chunks = []
    for start in tqdm(range(0, len(texts), batch_size), desc="BERT embeddings"):
        batch = [safe_text(x) for x in texts[start:start+batch_size]]
        tok = tokenizer(batch, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=max_length, return_tensors="pt")
        ids = tok["input_ids"].to(DEVICE); mask = tok["attention_mask"].to(DEVICE)
        with torch.no_grad():
            with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=(DEVICE.type=="cuda")):
                out = bert(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=mask).last_hidden_state[:,0,:]
        chunks.append(out.float().cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(chunks, axis=0).astype(np.float32)

class ListingImageDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, paths): self.paths = list(paths)
    def __len__(self): return len(self.paths)
    def __getitem__(self, i):
        try:
            with Image.open(self.paths[i]) as im: im = im.convert("RGB")
            return image_transform(im)
        except Exception:
            # Should be rare after image verification; a neutral ImageNet-normalized tensor is not used as a fake listing.
            raise RuntimeError(f"Could not read image: {self.paths[i]}")

def encode_images(paths, batch_size=BACKBONE_BATCH_SIZE):
    ds = ListingImageDataset(paths)
    dl = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False, num_workers=2, pin_memory=(DEVICE.type=="cuda"))
    chunks = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb in tqdm(dl, desc="MobileNet embeddings"):
            xb = xb.to(DEVICE, non_blocking=True)
            with torch.cuda.amp.autocast(enabled=(DEVICE.type=="cuda")):
                fmap = mobilenet.features(xb)
                pooled = nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(fmap, (1,1)).flatten(1)
            chunks.append(pooled.float().cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(chunks, axis=0).astype(np.float32)

all_df = pd.concat([train_df, val_df, test_df], ignore_index=True)

    np.savez_compressed(cache_path, text=X_text_all, image=X_image_all)

9. Train the seven modality combinations¶

The seven combinations mirror the paper's experimental design: metadata, text, image, metadata+text, metadata+image, text+image, and all three modalities. Each combination gets its own trainable fusion/regression head. Backbones remain frozen and shared.

In [12]:
class FusionRegressor(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, tab_dim, active=("tab","text","image"), dropout=0.25):
        super().__init__()
        self.active = tuple(active)
        self.tab_branch = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(tab_dim,128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(128,64), nn.ReLU())
        self.text_branch = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(768,128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(128,64), nn.ReLU())
        self.image_branch = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1280,128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(128,64), nn.ReLU())
        self.regressor = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64*len(self.active),128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Dropout(dropout), nn.Linear(128,64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64,1))
    def forward(self, tab, text, image):
        parts=[]
        if "tab" in self.active: parts.append(self.tab_branch(tab))
        if "text" in self.active: parts.append(self.text_branch(text))
        if "image" in self.active: parts.append(self.image_branch(image))
        return self.regressor(torch.cat(parts, dim=1)).squeeze(1)

modalities = {
    "Metadata": ("tab",),
    "Text": ("text",),
    "Image": ("image",),
    "Metadata + Text": ("tab","text"),
    "Metadata + Image": ("tab","image"),
    "Text + Image": ("text","image"),
    "Metadata + Text + Image": ("tab","text","image"),
}

train_tensors = (torch.tensor(X_train_tab), torch.tensor(X_train_text), torch.tensor(X_train_image), torch.tensor(y_train))
val_tensors = (torch.tensor(X_val_tab), torch.tensor(X_val_text), torch.tensor(X_val_image), torch.tensor(y_val))
test_tensors = (torch.tensor(X_test_tab), torch.tensor(X_test_text), torch.tensor(X_test_image), torch.tensor(y_test))
train_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(*train_tensors), batch_size=HEAD_BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=True)
val_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(*val_tensors), batch_size=HEAD_BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False)

def train_head(active, name):
    model = FusionRegressor(X_train_tab.shape[1], active=active).to(DEVICE)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=LEARNING_RATE, weight_decay=WEIGHT_DECAY)
    scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(optimizer, mode="min", factor=.5, patience=2)
    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    best_state, best_val, wait = None, float("inf"), 0
    history = {"train_loss":[], "val_loss":[]}
    for epoch in range(1, HEAD_EPOCHS+1):
        model.train(); tr_losses=[]
        for tb,tx,im,y in train_loader:
            tb=tb.to(DEVICE); tx=tx.to(DEVICE); im=im.to(DEVICE); y=y.to(DEVICE)
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            pred=model(tb,tx,im); loss=loss_fn(pred,y)
            loss.backward(); torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 2.0); optimizer.step()
            tr_losses.append(loss.item())
        model.eval(); va_losses=[]
        with torch.no_grad():
            for tb,tx,im,y in val_loader:
                tb=tb.to(DEVICE); tx=tx.to(DEVICE); im=im.to(DEVICE); y=y.to(DEVICE)
                va_losses.append(loss_fn(model(tb,tx,im),y).item())
        tr=float(np.mean(tr_losses)); va=float(np.mean(va_losses)); scheduler.step(va)
        history["train_loss"].append(tr); history["val_loss"].append(va)
        if va < best_val - 1e-5:
            best_val=va; best_state={k:v.detach().cpu().clone() for k,v in model.state_dict().items()}; wait=0
        else: wait += 1
        if epoch==1 or epoch%5==0:
            print(f"{name} | epoch {epoch:02d} | train {tr:.4f} | val {va:.4f}")
        if wait >= HEAD_PATIENCE: break
    model.load_state_dict(best_state); model.to(DEVICE); model.eval()
    torch.save({"state_dict":model.state_dict(),"active":active,"history":history}, ARTIFACT_DIR/f"{name.lower().replace(' ','_').replace('+','plus')}.pt")
    return model, history, best_val

models_by_subset, histories, val_losses = {}, {}, {}
for name, active in modalities.items():
    print("\nTraining:", name)
    m,h,v = train_head(active, name)
    models_by_subset[name]=m; histories[name]=h; val_losses[name]=v
    gc.collect()
    if DEVICE.type=="cuda": torch.cuda.empty_cache()

10. Final test evaluation¶

All seven model variants are selected using validation loss only. The test set is used once for the final comparison. Metrics are reported in the original price unit as supplied by Inside Airbnb (the raw file's currency convention); this notebook does not convert currencies.

In [13]:
def predict_log(model, tab, text, image, batch_size=512):
    model.eval(); outs=[]
    with torch.no_grad():
        for start in range(0,len(tab),batch_size):
            sl=slice(start,start+batch_size)
            pred=model(torch.tensor(tab[sl],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE),
                       torch.tensor(text[sl],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE),
                       torch.tensor(image[sl],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE))
            outs.append(pred.detach().cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(outs)

def regression_metrics(y_true_price, y_pred_price):
    return {
        "MAE": mean_absolute_error(y_true_price,y_pred_price),
        "RMSE": mean_squared_error(y_true_price,y_pred_price)**0.5,
        "R2": r2_score(y_true_price,y_pred_price),
        "MAPE_%": np.mean(np.abs((y_true_price-y_pred_price)/np.maximum(y_true_price,1e-6)))*100
    }

y_test_price = test_df["price_target"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
results=[]; test_predictions={}
for name, model in models_by_subset.items():
    pred_log=predict_log(model,X_test_tab,X_test_text,X_test_image)
    pred_price=np.maximum(0,np.expm1(pred_log))
    test_predictions[name]=pred_price
    results.append({"Model":name, **regression_metrics(y_test_price,pred_price), "Validation log-MSE":val_losses[name]})
results_df=pd.DataFrame(results).sort_values("MAE")
display(results_df.round(4))
results_df.to_csv(ARTIFACT_DIR/"modality_comparison.csv",index=False)

11. Evaluate the incremental value of each modality¶

A multimodal model is not automatically better. Compare it against the validation-selected unimodal and bimodal alternatives. Discuss both MAE and RMSE/R²: a tiny MAE improvement accompanied by worse RMSE or R² is not strong evidence that the third modality helps.

12. Global and local XAI — SHAP for metadata¶

We explain the tabular contribution conditional on one listing's text and image embeddings. Kernel SHAP perturbs the transformed tabular vector while holding the selected listing's text/image representations fixed. This is a local, conditional explanation of the multimodal model, not a causal effect and not a global explanation of all three modalities.

In [15]:
import shap

# Use a small SHAP background/explanation set for a T4-friendly Kernel SHAP run.
rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
bg_n = min(SHAP_BACKGROUND, len(X_train_tab))
bg_idx = rng.choice(len(X_train_tab), size=bg_n, replace=False)
shap_bg = X_train_tab[bg_idx]
explain_n = min(SHAP_EXPLAIN_ROWS, len(X_test_tab))
explain_idx = rng.choice(len(X_test_tab), size=explain_n, replace=False)

shap_values_all=[]
for local_pos, test_i in enumerate(explain_idx):
    fixed_text = X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1]
    fixed_image = X_test_image[test_i:test_i+1]
    def tabular_predict(z):
        z=np.asarray(z,dtype=np.float32)
        tx=np.repeat(fixed_text,len(z),axis=0)
        im=np.repeat(fixed_image,len(z),axis=0)
        p=predict_log(full_model,z,tx,im)
        return np.expm1(p)
    explainer=shap.KernelExplainer(tabular_predict,shap_bg)
    sv=explainer.shap_values(X_test_tab[test_i:test_i+1],nsamples=min(300,2*X_test_tab.shape[1]+100),silent=True)
    sv=np.asarray(sv)
    if sv.ndim==3: sv=sv[0]
    if sv.ndim==2: sv=sv[0]
    shap_values_all.append(sv)

shap_values_all=np.asarray(shap_values_all)
mean_abs_shap=np.mean(np.abs(shap_values_all),axis=0)
shap_importance=pd.DataFrame({"feature":tab_feature_names,"mean_abs_shap":mean_abs_shap}).sort_values("mean_abs_shap",ascending=False)

13. Global XAI — Partial Dependence Plot (PDP)¶

PDP answers: on average, how does the model's predicted price change when one metadata feature is varied? We use a sample of test rows and keep each row's text/image embedding fixed. Correlated features can make PDP unrealistic; interpret the curve as a model sensitivity analysis, not a causal effect.

In [16]:
def partial_dependence_numeric(feature, grid_size=12, sample_size=120):
    if feature not in numeric_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"{feature} is not an available numeric metadata feature. Available: {numeric_cols}")
    sample_n=min(sample_size,len(test_df))
    ids=rng.choice(len(test_df),size=sample_n,replace=False)
    raw_base=test_df.iloc[ids].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
    q=np.nanquantile(raw_base[feature].astype(float),np.linspace(.05,.95,grid_size))
    means=[]; stds=[]
    for value in q:
        modified=raw_base.copy(); modified[feature]=value
        x_tab=np.asarray(preprocessor.transform(modified),dtype=np.float32)
        pred=np.expm1(predict_log(full_model,x_tab,X_test_text[ids],X_test_image[ids]))
        means.append(float(np.mean(pred))); stds.append(float(np.std(pred)))
    return q,np.asarray(means),np.asarray(stds)

pdp_feature = "accommodates" if "accommodates" in numeric_cols else numeric_cols[0]
pdp_x,pdp_mean,pdp_std=partial_dependence_numeric(pdp_feature)
plt.figure(figsize=(7,4)); plt.plot(pdp_x,pdp_mean,marker="o"); plt.fill_between(pdp_x,pdp_mean-pdp_std,pdp_mean+pdp_std,alpha=.18)
plt.xlabel(pdp_feature); plt.ylabel("Average predicted nightly price"); plt.title(f"PDP — {pdp_feature}"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

14. Local text explanations — LIME¶

LIME perturbs the text of one listing while keeping its metadata and image fixed. It fits a local interpretable surrogate around that listing. Its result is sensitive to perturbation sampling, so we report it as a local explanation rather than a global word-importance ranking.

In [18]:
from lime.lime_text import LimeTextExplainer

sample_i = int(explain_idx[0])

fixed_tab = X_test_tab[sample_i:sample_i+1]
fixed_img = X_test_image[sample_i:sample_i+1]


# LIME calls this function with a list of perturbed texts.
# We return one continuous price prediction per text.
def predict_text_variants(text_list):

    text_list = list(text_list)

    emb = encode_texts(text_list, batch_size=24)

    tabs = np.repeat(fixed_tab, len(text_list), axis=0)
    imgs = np.repeat(fixed_img, len(text_list), axis=0)

    predictions_log = predict_log(
        full_model, tabs, emb, imgs
    )

    predictions_price = np.expm1(predictions_log)

    predictions_price = np.asarray(
        predictions_price, dtype=np.float64
    ).reshape(-1)

    if len(predictions_price) != len(text_list):
        raise ValueError("Prediction batch size mismatch.")

    if not np.all(np.isfinite(predictions_price)):
        raise ValueError("Non-finite price predictions detected.")

    # LimeTextExplainer expects a 2D output:
    # (number of perturbed texts, number of outputs).
    return predictions_price.reshape(-1, 1)


# LimeTextExplainer has no native mode='regression' argument.
# We use one continuous output column and explain output index 0.
lime_explainer = LimeTextExplainer(
    bow=True,
    random_state=SEED
)

lime_exp = lime_explainer.explain_instance(
    test_df.iloc[sample_i]["text_input"],
    predict_text_variants,
    labels=(0,),
    num_features=12,
    num_samples=LIME_NUM_SAMPLES
)

# Display the local word contributions
lime_weights = lime_exp.as_list(label=0)

print("Listing index:", sample_i)
print(
    "Actual price:",
    float(y_test_price[sample_i]),
    "AUD"
)
print(
    "Predicted price:",
    float(test_predictions[full_name][sample_i]),
    "AUD"
)

print("\nLIME local word contributions:")

for word, weight in lime_weights:
    print(f"{word:30s} {weight:+.4f} AUD")

# Plot without the misleading classification label
words = [item[0] for item in lime_weights]
weights = [item[1] for item in lime_weights]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))

colors = [
    "seagreen" if w > 0 else "indianred"
    for w in weights
]

ax.barh(words[::-1], weights[::-1], color=colors[::-1])

ax.axvline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Local contribution to predicted price (AUD)")
ax.set_title("LIME – Local Text Explanation for Airbnb Price")

15. Local text explanations — Integrated Gradients¶

Integrated Gradients attributes the model's log-price output to input token embeddings. The baseline uses PAD embeddings with the same attention mask. This is a gradient-based attribution for the BERT branch, with the tabular and image embeddings held fixed.

In [19]:
def integrated_gradients_text(text, tab_vec, image_vec, steps=24):
    tok=tokenizer(text,return_tensors="pt",truncation=True,max_length=MAX_TEXT_LENGTH,padding="max_length")
    ids=tok["input_ids"].to(DEVICE); mask=tok["attention_mask"].to(DEVICE)
    input_emb=bert.embeddings.word_embeddings(ids).detach()
    pad_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id if tokenizer.pad_token_id is not None else 0
    base_ids=torch.full_like(ids,pad_id)
    base_emb=bert.embeddings.word_embeddings(base_ids).detach()
    delta=input_emb-base_emb
    tab=torch.tensor(tab_vec,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE).reshape(1,-1)
    img=torch.tensor(image_vec,dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE).reshape(1,-1)
    grad_sum=torch.zeros_like(input_emb)
    full_model.eval()
    for alpha in torch.linspace(0,1,steps,device=DEVICE):
        x=(base_emb+alpha*delta).detach().requires_grad_(True)
        out=bert(inputs_embeds=x,attention_mask=mask).last_hidden_state[:,0,:]
        pred=full_model(tab,out,img)
        grad=torch.autograd.grad(pred.sum(),x)[0]
        grad_sum += grad.detach()
    avg_grad=grad_sum/steps
    token_attr=(delta*avg_grad).sum(dim=-1).squeeze(0).detach().cpu().numpy()
    tokens=tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids.squeeze(0).detach().cpu().tolist())
    valid=mask.squeeze(0).detach().cpu().numpy().astype(bool)
    pairs=[(t,float(a)) for t,a,v in zip(tokens,token_attr,valid) if v and t not in ["[CLS]","[SEP]","[PAD]"]]
    return sorted(pairs,key=lambda x:abs(x[1]),reverse=True), pairs

ig_top, ig_all=integrated_gradients_text(test_df.iloc[sample_i]["text_input"],fixed_tab[0],fixed_img[0])
print("Top Integrated Gradients tokens:")
for token,score in ig_top[:15]: print(f"{token:22s} {score:+.5f}")

16. Local image explanations — Grad-CAM¶

Grad-CAM uses gradients of the predicted log price with respect to the final MobileNetV2 convolutional feature map. The heatmap indicates image regions that most influence the regression output; it does not establish that those regions causally determine market price.

In [20]:
def load_image_tensor(path):
    with Image.open(path) as im: return image_transform(im.convert("RGB")).unsqueeze(0).to(DEVICE)

def gradcam_for_listing(test_i):
    image_tensor=load_image_tensor(test_df.iloc[test_i]["image_path"]).requires_grad_(True)
    activation_box={}
    def forward_hook(module, inputs, output):
        activation_box["activation"]=output
    handle=mobilenet.features[-1].register_forward_hook(forward_hook)
    tab=torch.tensor(X_test_tab[test_i:test_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    txt=torch.tensor(X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    mobilenet.zero_grad(set_to_none=True); full_model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    fmap=mobilenet.features(image_tensor)
    activation_box["activation"]=fmap
    img_feat=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(fmap,(1,1)).flatten(1)
    pred=full_model(tab,txt,img_feat)
    grads=torch.autograd.grad(pred.sum(),fmap)[0]
    weights=grads.mean(dim=(2,3),keepdim=True)
    cam=torch.relu((weights*fmap).sum(dim=1,keepdim=True))
    cam=nn.functional.interpolate(cam,size=(224,224),mode="bilinear",align_corners=False)
    cam=cam.squeeze().detach().cpu().numpy()
    cam=(cam-cam.min())/(cam.max()-cam.min()+1e-8)
    handle.remove()
    return image_tensor.detach().cpu().squeeze().permute(1,2,0).numpy(),cam,float(pred.detach().cpu().item())

img_norm,cam,log_pred=gradcam_for_listing(sample_i)
# Denormalize ImageNet normalization for display.
mean=np.array([.485,.456,.406]); std=np.array([.229,.224,.225])
img_display=np.clip(img_norm*std+mean,0,1)
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(10,4))
ax[0].imshow(img_display); ax[0].set_title("Original listing image"); ax[0].axis("off")
ax[1].imshow(img_display); ax[1].imshow(cam,cmap="jet",alpha=.42); ax[1].set_title("Grad-CAM — price regression"); ax[1].axis("off")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

17. Image explanations — Occlusion sensitivity¶

We replace image patches with the normalized-image mean (zero in normalized space) and measure the change in predicted price, with text and tabular inputs fixed. Large absolute changes indicate sensitivity to the occluded patch.

In [21]:
def image_occlusion(test_i, patch=32, stride=32):
    x=load_image_tensor(test_df.iloc[test_i]["image_path"])
    tab=torch.tensor(X_test_tab[test_i:test_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    txt=torch.tensor(X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    with torch.no_grad():
        base_feat=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(mobilenet.features(x),(1,1)).flatten(1)
        base_pred=full_model(tab,txt,base_feat).item()
    heat=np.zeros((224,224),dtype=np.float32); count=np.zeros_like(heat)
    for y in range(0,224-patch+1,stride):
        for xx in range(0,224-patch+1,stride):
            oc=x.clone(); oc[:,:,y:y+patch,xx:xx+patch]=0.0
            with torch.no_grad():
                feat=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(mobilenet.features(oc),(1,1)).flatten(1)
                pred=full_model(tab,txt,feat).item()
            heat[y:y+patch,xx:xx+patch]+=abs(pred-base_pred)
            count[y:y+patch,xx:xx+patch]+=1
    heat/=np.maximum(count,1)
    return heat,base_pred

occ_heat,base_pred=image_occlusion(sample_i)
plt.figure(figsize=(6,5)); plt.imshow(img_display); plt.imshow(occ_heat,cmap="magma",alpha=.48); plt.title("Image occlusion sensitivity"); plt.axis("off"); plt.show()

18. Multimodal explainability — exact Shapley values over three modalities¶

For one listing, compute all 8 coalitions of {metadata, text, image}. A missing modality is replaced by the training-set mean embedding for that branch. Exact Shapley values then decompose the prediction difference from the all-baseline prediction. These are model-output attributions, not causal effects. The baseline choice matters and must be stated.

In [22]:
from itertools import combinations

train_tab_mean=np.mean(X_train_tab,axis=0,keepdims=True)
train_text_mean=np.mean(X_train_text,axis=0,keepdims=True)
train_image_mean=np.mean(X_train_image,axis=0,keepdims=True)
players=["tab","text","image"]

def coalition_value(test_i, coalition):
    tb=X_test_tab[test_i:test_i+1] if "tab" in coalition else train_tab_mean
    tx=X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1] if "text" in coalition else train_text_mean
    im=X_test_image[test_i:test_i+1] if "image" in coalition else train_image_mean
    return float(predict_log(full_model,tb,tx,im)[0])

def exact_modality_shapley(test_i):
    values={}
    for r in range(4):
        for comb in combinations(players,r): values[frozenset(comb)]=coalition_value(test_i,set(comb))
    phi={}
    n=len(players)
    import math as _math
    for m in players:
        total=0.0
        others=[x for x in players if x!=m]
        for r in range(n):
            for comb in combinations(others,r):
                S=frozenset(comb)
                weight=_math.factorial(r)*_math.factorial(n-r-1)/_math.factorial(n)
                total += weight*(values[S|{m}]-values[S])
        phi[m]=total
    return values,phi

coalition_vals, modality_phi=exact_modality_shapley(sample_i)
print("Coalition predictions (log-price scale):")
for k,v in coalition_vals.items(): print(sorted(k) if k else "EMPTY", round(v,5))
print("Exact modality Shapley values:", modality_phi)
print("Efficiency check (sum phi vs full - baseline):", sum(modality_phi.values()), coalition_vals[frozenset(players)]-coalition_vals[frozenset()])
plt.figure(figsize=(6,3)); plt.bar(list(modality_phi.keys()),list(modality_phi.values())); plt.axhline(0,color="black",linewidth=.8); plt.ylabel("Shapley contribution (log price)"); plt.title("Local modality contributions"); plt.show()

19. Local faithfulness checks¶

These deletion tests measure whether removing highly attributed input elements changes the model output more than removing random elements. They are sanity checks, not proof of causal relevance. Text uses IG-ranked tokens; images use the occlusion map; metadata uses SHAP-ranked transformed features.

In [23]:
# Text deletion: replace top-attribution words with [MASK] while preserving the other modalities.
text_original=test_df.iloc[sample_i]["text_input"]
words=re.findall(r"\b\w+\b",text_original)
top_tokens=[t.replace("##","").lower() for t,_ in ig_top[:8]]

def mask_words(text, terms):
    out=text
    for term in terms:
        if term:
            out=re.sub(re.escape(term),"[MASK]",out,flags=re.IGNORECASE,count=1)
    return out

if words:
    masked=mask_words(text_original,top_tokens)
    p0=float(predict_text_variants([text_original])[0])
    p_top=float(predict_text_variants([masked])[0])
    rand_terms=random.sample(words,min(8,len(words)))
    p_rand=float(predict_text_variants([mask_words(text_original,rand_terms)])[0])
    print("Text deletion |prediction change| top IG:",abs(p0-p_top))
    print("Text deletion |prediction change| random words:",abs(p0-p_rand))

# Image deletion: occlude the most sensitive 10% of pixels and compare with random locations.
heat=occ_heat.copy(); k=max(1,int(.10*heat.size)); top_flat=np.argpartition(heat.ravel(),-k)[-k:]
mask=np.zeros(heat.size,dtype=bool); mask[top_flat]=True; mask=mask.reshape(224,224)
x=load_image_tensor(test_df.iloc[sample_i]["image_path"])
x_top=x.clone(); x_top[:,:,torch.tensor(mask,device=DEVICE)]=0
# Random pixel mask with exactly k entries.
rand_flat=rng.choice(heat.size,size=k,replace=False); rand_mask=np.zeros(heat.size,dtype=bool); rand_mask[rand_flat]=True; rand_mask=rand_mask.reshape(224,224)
x_rand=x.clone(); x_rand[:,:,torch.tensor(rand_mask,device=DEVICE)]=0
with torch.no_grad():
    tb=torch.tensor(X_test_tab[sample_i:sample_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    tx=torch.tensor(X_test_text[sample_i:sample_i+1],dtype=torch.float32,device=DEVICE)
    f0=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(mobilenet.features(x),(1,1)).flatten(1)
    ft=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(mobilenet.features(x_top),(1,1)).flatten(1)
    fr=nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool2d(mobilenet.features(x_rand),(1,1)).flatten(1)
    pv0=full_model(tb,tx,f0).item(); pvt=full_model(tb,tx,ft).item(); pvr=full_model(tb,tx,fr).item()
print("Image deletion |log-price change| top occlusion:",abs(pv0-pvt))
print("Image deletion |log-price change| random:",abs(pv0-pvr))

20. Counterfactual what-if explanation (tabular features)¶

We search for a real training-set profile with the same room type and use its observed capacity tuple (accommodates, bedrooms, beds, bathrooms_numeric) as a feasible candidate intervention on the selected listing. Text and image are held fixed. The nearest candidate that changes the predicted price by at least 10% is reported. This is a model what-if explanation, not a causal recommendation: changing capacity may require changing the real property, description, and image as well.

In [24]:
CONTROLLABLE = [c for c in ["accommodates", "bedrooms", "beds", "bathrooms_numeric"] if c in numeric_cols]

def find_tabular_counterfactual(test_i, target_relative_change=0.10, max_candidates=500):
    if not CONTROLLABLE:
        print("No suitable capacity features are available for a constrained counterfactual.")
        return None
    original = test_df.iloc[test_i].copy()
    room_value = original.get("room_type", None)
    candidates = train_df.copy()
    if "room_type" in candidates.columns and pd.notna(room_value):
        same_room = candidates[candidates["room_type"].astype(str) == str(room_value)]
        if len(same_room) >= 20:
            candidates = same_room
    candidates = candidates.dropna(subset=CONTROLLABLE)
    if len(candidates) > max_candidates:
        candidates = candidates.sample(max_candidates, random_state=SEED)
    original_frame = pd.DataFrame([original])
    x0 = np.asarray(preprocessor.transform(original_frame), dtype=np.float32)
    p0 = float(np.expm1(predict_log(full_model, x0, X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1], X_test_image[test_i:test_i+1])[0]))
    scales = train_df[CONTROLLABLE].astype(float).std().replace(0, 1).fillna(1)
    found = []
    for _, donor in candidates.iterrows():
        modified = original.copy()
        for col in CONTROLLABLE:
            modified[col] = donor[col]
        # Keep all other metadata and both non-tabular modalities fixed.
        x1 = np.asarray(preprocessor.transform(pd.DataFrame([modified])), dtype=np.float32)
        p1 = float(np.expm1(predict_log(full_model, x1, X_test_text[test_i:test_i+1], X_test_image[test_i:test_i+1])[0]))
        if p1 <= p0 * (1-target_relative_change):
            changed = [c for c in CONTROLLABLE if not np.isclose(float(original[c]), float(modified[c]), equal_nan=True)]
            distance = sum(abs(float(original[c])-float(modified[c]))/float(scales[c]) for c in CONTROLLABLE)
            found.append((distance, p1, modified, changed))
    if not found:
        print(f"No observed capacity profile achieved a {target_relative_change:.0%} lower prediction while other modalities were fixed.")
        print("This is a valid negative result: the selected counterfactual search did not find a feasible profile.")
        return None
    found.sort(key=lambda z:z[0])
    distance, p1, best, changed = found[0]
    print(f"Original predicted price: {p0:.2f}")
    print(f"Counterfactual predicted price: {p1:.2f} ({(p1/p0-1)*100:.1f}% change)")
    print("Changed capacity fields:")
    for c in changed: print(f"  {c}: {original[c]} -> {best[c]}")
    print(f"Normalized edit distance: {distance:.4f}")
    print("Interpretation: model-conditional what-if only; not a causal or operational recommendation.")
    return {"original_prediction":p0,"counterfactual_prediction":p1,"changed_features":changed,"distance":distance}

cf_result = find_tabular_counterfactual(sample_i)

22. Interpretation guide for the oral presentation¶

Use the actual values from modality_comparison.csv and the plots generated above. Do not claim multimodal superiority unless the full model improves the preselected validation/test criteria consistently.

Suggested interpretation points:

  • Metadata: captures property capacity, room type, amenities, host and location attributes.
  • Text: captures qualitative descriptions not fully represented by structured columns.
  • Image: may capture visible quality, room layout, light, furnishing and interior characteristics; its marginal value must be empirically verified.
  • SHAP: indicates which transformed metadata features influence a particular price prediction, conditional on fixed text/image embeddings.
  • PDP: summarizes average model sensitivity to a selected metadata variable, not a causal effect.
  • LIME / Integrated Gradients: identify text tokens influential to one listing's predicted price; explanations can be unstable and are model-dependent.
  • Grad-CAM / Occlusion: identify image regions whose visual features influence the model output; the heatmap is not a guarantee of semantic understanding.
  • Modality Shapley: decomposes one prediction relative to the chosen mean-embedding baseline. It is not a causal contribution.

Limitations to state clearly¶

  1. This uses a newer publicly downloadable snapshot than the paper's April 2024 collection.
  2. The paper's 8,380-row sample and reported scores cannot be exactly reproduced without the authors' exact snapshot and scraping pipeline.
  3. picture_url downloads can fail or be rate-limited; report actual image coverage.
  4. The target is a displayed nightly listing price, not a confirmed transaction price and not an event-venue quote.
  5. A single-city study in Amsterdam cannot be directly generalized to Tunis.
  6. Reputation variables may be contemporaneous/post-outcome; interpret them as predictive correlates, not causal price drivers.
  7. Frozen pretrained encoders plus trained fusion heads are a T4-friendly adaptation, not identical to full end-to-end fine-tuning.

References¶

  • Tan, H., Su, T., Wu, X., Cheng, P., & Zheng, T. (2024). A Sustainable Rental Price Prediction Model Based on Multimodal Input and Deep Learning—Evidence from Airbnb. Sustainability, 16(15), 6384. https://doi.org/10.3390/su16156384
  • Inside Airbnb. Get the Data. https://insideairbnb.com/get-the-data/ (CC BY 4.0; cite the exact snapshot date used).
